api: ExpandItem.setControl/setHeight/setExpanded, ExpandBar layout; Control.getBounds of the item control
stock_behaviour: an item control whose logical y is beyond 32767 px is placed at y 32767 (Windows clamps child windows to the 16-bit range): getBounds answers 32767 and the control is shown under the wrong item when scrolled into view
our_behaviour: the control keeps its logical position (ViewportPlane, Composite viewport L1): getBounds answers it and the control is shown under its item
cause_stock_file_line: ExpandItem.java:426-427 (control.setBoundsInPixels / setLocationInPixels at y + header) -> Control.java:3298 (OS.SetWindowPos), official 3.135.0
javadoc_quote: Control.setLocation: "Sets the receiver's location to the point specified by the arguments which are relative to the receiver's parent"; Control.getBounds: "Returns a rectangle describing the receiver's size and location in points relative to its parent"
accepted_by: Test_org_eclipse_swt_widgets_ExpandBar_ViewportDifferential.LOGICAL_WHERE_STOCK_CLAMPS (control y and in-range move count, only where the stock line has a control off its logical position or at/beyond the native edge, and the viewport line has every control logical); Test_org_eclipse_swt_widgets_ExpandBar_Viewport

api: scrolling: vertical scroll bar, mouse wheel, keyboard focus (WM_VSCROLL, WM_MOUSEWHEEL, showFocus)
stock_behaviour: ScrollWindowEx (SW_SCROLLCHILDREN) moves the child windows natively: a control beyond the native range moves from its clamped position (for example to 32773 instead of 41702), so it is neither at its item nor at the clamp
our_behaviour: the same native scroll, then every child that did not move by the scroll amount moves there logically (ExpandBar.scrollWindow)
cause_stock_file_line: ExpandBar.java:862 (wmScroll) and ExpandBar.java:632 (showFocus): OS.ScrollWindowEx (handle, 0, updateY, null, null, 0, null, OS.SW_SCROLLCHILDREN | OS.SW_INVALIDATE), official 3.135.0
javadoc_quote: ExpandItem.setControl: "Sets the control that is shown when the item is expanded."; Control.getBounds: "Returns a rectangle describing the receiver's size and location in points relative to its parent"
accepted_by: same relation as D1 (the differential scrolls with WM_VSCROLL and the wheel); Test_org_eclipse_swt_widgets_ExpandBar_Viewport (end, back to the top)
